observed_behavior: A peer branch commit invalidates an unchanged caller's reference QA publication.
expected_behavior: Worktree-scoped QA depends only on caller HEAD and content; explicit repository indexing retains shared-ref validation.
causal_mechanism: A local commit gate refreshed and fenced every shared branch and tag, making independent worker progress an availability dependency.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A local validation gate inherits a repository-wide mutable-state boundary.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Independent linked worktrees share refs and therefore invalidate each other's otherwise valid publications.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Publication stability matches the selected query scope without weakening caller-state validation.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Select worktree scope in the canonical refresh for QA and current-worktree queries; fence caller HEAD and overlay content before transaction commit.

applicability_conditions: Independent linked Git worktrees share mutable refs.
known_non_matches: Explicit repository maintenance intentionally observes and validates every shared ref.
confirmation_evidence: The real PostgreSQL linked-worktree regression failed on peer ref movement before the fix and passes afterward.
regression_proofs: tests/repository-index-concurrency.test.js: worktree indexing tolerates peer commits while fencing caller HEAD and content
